previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with persistent epigastric pain and pain at the PICC site, following a recent hospitalization for gastritis treated with IV pantoprazole via PICC. Blood work was stable, ultrasound showed no DVT, and blood cultures were negative for infection. Given lack of symptom improvement on IV therapy, the PICC was removed and the patient was transitioned to oral pantoprazole. She tolerated a stage III bariatric diet and tube feeds, with improvement in symptoms. She was discharged home with oral medications and follow-up instructions. The hospital course was uncomplicated.

ACTIVE ISSUES 
=========

#Abdominal pain: She presented with burning abdominal pain, 
similar to her chronic pain. The etiology of her pain was 
thought to be multifactorial in the setting of multiple 
abdominal surgeries, with possible component so dysmotility, 
reflux, and bacterial overgrowth. She was evaluated by Bariatric 
surgery in the ED who recommended admission to medicine for pain 
control, without the need for surgical intervention. She had 
normal labs, without electrolyte abnormalities. KUB was negative 
for any obstruction. She continued to have normal non-bloody, 
bowel movements. She was continued on tube feeds at goal this 
admission. She was initially NPO but advanced to clears and full 
liquids, tolerating cream of wheat and some pudding, in addition 
to water. She did not have further episodes of emesis. She was 
trailed on erythromycin and rifaximin was added on discharge for 
the possibility of bacterial overgrowth. Ranitidine was added 
for increased reflux management. H. pylori serology was tested, 
with results pending at the time of discharge. Her abdominal 
pain stabilized and she was discharged with close follow up in 
the Bariatric Surgery Clinic on ___.

During her admission, the treatment team had a long discussion 
about the etiology of her pain and set expectations that 
unfortunately her pain was unlikely to resolve completely over 
the short term. She was understanding that this would require a 
team based effort amongst her outpatient providers to establish 
a regimen that works for her and allows her to regain some 
quality of life. She was encouraged to continue with tube feeds 
at home and PO intake (water/ensure shakes) and gradually add in 
solid foods slowly over weeks to months as tolerated. The team 
discussed that the new medications erythromycin and rifaximin 
might take some time to work and that she should discuss whether 
to continue these medications at her outpatient appointment on 
___ with Dr. ___. She was in agreement 
with this plan
